analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. The patch bumps the "Last updated" date and clarifies the sample_age_ms semantics for performance measurements. Age is now elapsed time since the newest observation, even if an older completed observation arrives later. The patch also adds a note that the Swift producer applies the same rule to each workload bucket and current-posture series (EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift), with the EWMA and sample counts unchanged and no wire-field changes. The supplied units are base text beyond the changed ranges (lines 588-1404). These are unchanged surrounding protocol documentation, and I saw no new or changed content there.

Security relevance is limited. These are transient capacity and performance fields used for routing and scheduling. The adjacent documentation says they cannot certify profiles, change memory reservations, or affect billing. The age semantics are a freshness control. They help stop stale samples from appearing fresh. The documented rule is not weaker than before. It applies freshness from the newest observation, so an out-of-order older completion cannot rejuvenate a sample.

No change to the authorization, attestation, encryption, or data-exposure boundaries (TB-002, TB-011, A-001, A-016, T-041) is visible. No code was supplied. Whether the Swift producer actually implements the documented rule, and whether the Go coordinator validates freshness consistently with it, is outside the supplied evidence. That is an integration question for a code-level pass rather than a finding.
